subject: Prompt data qualification + PII matrix — recap & next steps
body:
Message 1
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@medqorp.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Questions on what Redwood stores for prompts/outputs (PII)

Avery / Marissa —

Thanks for the call this morning. A couple of follow-up questions from our security team so we can finish our internal qualification checklist:

1) For text prompts sent to the API, are the raw inputs stored at rest by default?
2) Are generated outputs (model responses) retained by Redwood? If so, what is the default retention window and can it be configured per-account?
3) Where is any retained data stored (regions / physical residency)? We need to confirm EU-only storage for our EU customers.
4) Are prompt/response logs included in audit logs or admin console exports?
5) Can Redwood disable storage of prompt/output payloads for enterprise/private deployments?

Can you send over a short matrix and any existing SOC / compliance docs we can share with procurement? Attaching the SOC questionnaire we use.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Olivia Grant
Director of AI Ops
MedQorp
[Attachment: SOC2_request.pdf]

---
Message 2
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@medqorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood stores for prompts/outputs (PII)

Olivia —

Great questions — thanks for sending the questionnaire. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so your security/procurement teams have what they need:

Summary answers (high level):
- Default behavior: by default, Redwood does not retain customer prompt/response content beyond short-term operational logs unless a customer opts into retention for features (e.g., evals, cached prefixes).
- Retention window: operational logs (metadata + minimal trace) retained 14–30 days depending on plan; explicit prompt/output retention for product features is configurable and opt-in.
- Residency: Hosted API defaults to region selection (US, EU); customers can require EU-only residency for all persisted artifacts on paid tiers.
- Audit exports: Yes — admin/export endpoints can include request metadata; full payload export is only available if the customer has enabled payload retention.
- Private & Dedicated: We offer an explicit "no-persist" option for Dedicated/Private deployments that disables prompt/output storage at rest.

What I'll attach:
- A concise PII qualification matrix that maps common prompt elements to where/if they're stored and retention controls (see attachment).
- Our SOC 2 Type II summary and link to the full report under NDA (we can supply the full PDF to security).

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached the PII matrix — review and call out any prompts you expect to be treated as high-sensitivity PII.
2) If you need EU-only residency, let us know which accounts/tenants need that flag; we can lock residency for persisted artifacts.
3) For procurement, we can provide a limited SOC2 disclosure under NDA; Marissa will coordinate.

I'll summarize this in a short doc and set up a 30-minute follow-up with Monica (our customer reliability lead) if you want a deeper technical walkthrough of storage/keys and KMS options.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-prompt-data-matrix.xlsx]

Message 3
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@medqorp.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, MedQorp Security <security@medqorp.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:27:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood stores for prompts/outputs (PII)

Thanks Avery — this is helpful. Couple follow-ups after a quick pass of the matrix: 

- When you say "operational logs (metadata + minimal trace)", can you specify what fields are included in metadata? E.g., IP, timestamp, request_id, model_name, token_count?
- For the "no-persist" option on Dedicated/Private, does that also disable prefix cache and KV caches used to speed up generation, or only the long-term prompt storage? Performance trade-offs would be good to understand.
- Our legal team asked whether Redwood supports a contractual clause to prohibit storing prompt/outputs for MedQorp production tenants (i.e., a data non-retention addendum). Is that standard?

If possible, can Monica or Marissa confirm the exact retention windows and default fields in an audit export so we can close out the security review this week?

Olivia

---
Message 4
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@medqorp.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood stores for prompts/outputs (PII)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Quick, specific answers below (pulled directly from our storage & audit docs):

1) Operational metadata fields (default audit logs): request_id, request_timestamp, model_variant, model_name, token_count, route_id, customer_tenant_id (hashed), latency_ms, status_code.
  - We do NOT include full client IP in persisted logs by default; IP is available in ephemeral network logs for 7 days for incident response.

2) "No-persist" option behavior:
  - For Dedicated and Private deployments, enabling no-persist disables persistent prompt/response storage and long-term prefix caching. Short-lived in-memory KV cache used for a single session/stream remains for inference but is not written to disk.
  - There is a measurable performance trade-off for workloads that rely on caching across requests (cold-start token overhead). We can run benchmarks with a similar workload if you want concrete numbers.

3) Contractual non-retention addendum:
  - Yes — for enterprise contracts we offer a data non-retention clause that disallows Redwood from persisting prompt/outputs for specified tenants. That clause is regularly included for customers requiring stricter custody. Procurement/Legal should coordinate with Marissa for the exact language.

4) Retention windows by channel (defaults & configurable):
  - Admin/operational logs (metadata only): 14 days (standard) — can be extended to 30/90 days on request for specific plans.
  - Prompt/output payloads (if enabled): default 30 days, configurable 0/30/90/365; can be set to 0 (no-persist) at account/tenant level.
  - Audit exports: include metadata fields above; payloads only included if customer enabled payload retention.

5) Residency & encryption:
  - Persisted artifacts are stored in region-specific object stores (US/EU). For EU-only residency we can pin storage to EU data centers and prevent cross-region replication.
  - All persisted data at rest is encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys for Private deployments; hosted customers can opt for customer-managed keys on enterprise plans.

Attachments we can provide today:
- redwood-prompt-data-matrix.xlsx (detailed mapping)
- redwood-soc2-type2.pdf (summary of SOC 2 controls) — full report available under NDA

Next steps I suggest:
- Marissa will send the procurement/contract addendum language and initiate an NDA for the SOC report.
- If you want, we can schedule a 30-min technical session (Monica + infra engineer) to run through no-persist performance implications and KMS setup.

Would you like that session tomorrow morning or Friday afternoon?

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-soc2-type2.pdf]
